text: Step 1. Gather and sort your treasures. With a grown-up, collect loose leaves, smooth stones and any approved twigs, flowers or petals. Sort them into little piles by colour, shape or size. Choose a flat place with enough space for your circles to grow. Your maker’s part. Sort leaves and stones into piles. Grown-up help. Check the materials and approve the making space.

Step 1. Gather and sort your treasures. With a grown-up, collect loose leaves, smooth stones and any approved twigs, flowers or petals. Sort them into little piles by colour, shape or size. Choose a flat place with enough space for your circles to grow. Your maker’s part. Little Makers. Sort leaves and stones into piles. Young Creators. Look for several pieces that can repeat in a pattern. Grown-up help. Check the materials and approve the making space.

Step 2. Choose a special centre. Put one favourite stone, leaf or flower in the middle of your space. Leave room around it for several rings. Turn it until it looks right to you; your mandala can be big, small or a little wonky. Your maker’s part. Place your favourite piece in the middle.

Step 3. Make a repeating first ring. Place a circle of leaves or stones around your centre. Repeat one kind of piece, or alternate two colours or shapes. Keep going until the ring meets itself. Leave little gaps so each piece is easy to see. Your maker’s part. Repeat a leaf or a stone all the way around.

Leave little gaps so each piece is easy to see. Your maker’s part. Try an alternating broad-leaf, narrow-leaf pattern.

Step 4. Grow another summer pattern. Add a new ring outside the first. Try stones between leaves, twigs like sun rays, or approved petals for splashes of colour. Change the repeating rule with each ring and use the materials you have. Stop whenever the design feels complete. Your maker’s part. Add a piece in each outside gap.

Change the repeating rule with each ring and use the materials you have. Stop whenever the design feels complete. Your maker’s part. Build an outer ring with a different colour or repeating rule.

Step 5. Make the pattern your own. Step back and look at your summer mandala. Move any pieces you like, add a border, or leave it beautifully simple. Show someone your repeating pattern and take a picture before the breeze changes it. Your maker’s part. Point out your favourite colour or shape. Grown-up help. Help photograph the design and restore the space afterwards.
